input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Compliant at the fallback; no redline and no counterparty comment. Customer convenience right is present in substance: Section 17(b) (p0118) lets Sparkling terminate "at any time" on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, conditioned only on ceasing use and certifying return or destruction of the Software. No cause, breach, default or other trigger is required, so the right is unconditional; the clause simply does not carry the labels "for convenience" or "without cause", which is why a keyword-based check reports "Customer convenience termination present: failed". That is a wording artefact and substance controls. Ninety days sits at the top of the fallback notice range (60-90 days), and no early-termination fee, penalty, forfeiture or acceleration attaches to the exit, which is better than the fallback tolerance of a fee up to three months' fees. No Vendor convenience right exists anywhere: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency events and material default uncured after thirty days (17(c), p0128), and the renewable one-year maintenance term in Section 10 gives Garman no at-will right to exit, suspend or decline service, so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on fewer than 90 days' notice) is absent. Section 17(a) (p0117) also keeps the Agreement and licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year committed term from which Sparkling needs an exit. Shortfalls against the preferred position are recorded as observations only, not escalated: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and 17(b) contains no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (the fee-return remedy at p0128 applies only on termination for Garman's default), with prepayment exposure limited by the annual maintenance cycle.
